transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Ravi Desai (Redwood Security), Maya Patel (AlphaHealth Head of Security), Liam Chen (AlphaHealth SRE), Priya Rao (AlphaHealth Compliance)

Summary:
Quick posture review focused on SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts, Trust Center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO integration (Okta), audit log retention and schema, and encryption/KMS questions. AlphaHealth wants to verify scoped systems, see control mappings, and confirm data residency and key management options for a pilot.

Topics:
- SOC 2 Type II coverage & recent report availability
- ISO 27001 certificate and scope
- Trust Center (how to request access)
- Controls mapping spreadsheet (Redwood controls -> cust controls)
- RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, Okta flow
- Audit logs: retention, export, format, access
- Encryption: at-rest, in-transit, KMS/HSM options and BYOK
- Data residency and VPC/private deployment notes

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, happy Valentine's day, I guess, um let's do quick intros, I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood Inference.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Hi Jordan, Maya here, Head of Security at AlphaHealth, with Priya and Liam.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Hi all.
[00:19] Liam Chen: Hey.
[00:22] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, Redwood SE, I mostly work on private deployments and infra.
[00:26] Ravi Desai: Ravi, security engineering on Redwood side, I'll try to answer the controls/KMS bits.
[00:30] Jordan Park: Great. We planned this as a posture review - mainly SOC 2 / ISO 27001, talk through Trust Center access and give you the controls mapping. We'll also cover RBAC/SSO and audit logs. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:45] Maya Patel: Sounds good. High level - AlphaHealth is evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will process PHI-ish metadata, so we need to confirm SOC 2 Type II and ISO scope, KMS options, and whether we can get a trust center view and mapping to our control framework.
[01:05] Jordan Park: Understood. Quick housekeeping: we have the SOC 2 Type II report from last quarter and our ISO 27001 cert - I will share links, and there's a Trust Center where we provide evidence access for signed NDA customers.
[01:20] Maya Patel: When you say Trust Center, is that self-serve? Do we need a formal request? We prefer in-house review with our GRC team.
[01:28] Sofia Martinez: Right now it's gated - we typically grant read-only access after a DPA + NDA and an access request. Jordan will send the process doc. The Trust Center includes SOC report, policies, and evidence indexes, not full raw artifacts.
[01:45] Priya Rao: Can you confirm the ISO scope? Is it across Hosted API only, or does it include Dedicated and Private deployments?
[01:53] Ravi Desai: Good q. ISO cert currently covers Redwood control plane and hosted inference service. Dedicated/reserved capacity has overlapping controls but some infra responsibilities differ; for Private on-prem deployments, customers manage some controls locally so scope varies. We'll detail that in the controls mapping.
[02:10] Liam Chen: For Dedicated, we need to know which pieces AlphaHealth would be responsible for, e.g., network configuration, key management if BYOK, etc.
[02:18] Sofia Martinez: Exactly. Our docs show the delineation: things like tenant-level RBAC, SSO integration, and customer-managed keys are in-customer scope for private. We'll provide a table.
[02:30] Maya Patel: Let's talk KMS: can you do BYOK with an HSM? We need HSM-backed keys for production PHI.
[02:38] Ravi Desai: Yes, we support KMS integrations with major cloud KMS and have HSM options via customer-managed keys. For hosted customers we offer a managed KMS with HSM-backed providers as well, but BYOK means you control rotation and key lifecycle. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[02:55] Maya Patel: And what about audit logs? Retention, access, exports? Our compliance needs 1 year immutable logs plus SIEM integration.
[03:05] Sofia Martinez: Our default audit log retention is 90 days in the hosted plan, but for enterprise Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and external export to your SIEM via secure streaming. We'll send a sample export schema and retention options.
[03:20] Liam Chen: Do logs include token-level traces or just request metadata? We need to ensure no sensitive content is logged.
[03:27] Ravi Desai: Our audit logs capture request metadata, auth events, admin activity, and error traces; we mask user-provided request content in the logs by default but can accommodate extra redaction for PHI workflows. We'll confirm exact fields in a sample export.
[03:45] Priya Rao: About RBAC and SSO — Okta is our IdP, SCIM provisioning, SAML for SSO. How mature is your SAML/SCIM support?
[03:53] Sofia Martinez: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0 for user provisioning and role mapping. We also have fine-grained RBAC (roles, perms per project/model/route). There are a few small naming differences in the console, sometimes transcripts call it 'Redood console' haha, but the functionality's there.
[04:15] Maya Patel: Great. For controls mapping, we need a row-for-row mapping to our internal control names. Will you map Redwood controls to ISO 27001 controls and SOC 2 criteria?
[04:24] Jordan Park: Yes, our standard deliverable is a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood control IDs -> SOC 2 CC/CCM / ISO 27001 clause mapping and notes on responsibility split. Sofia and Ravi will prepare a draft.
[04:35] Priya Rao: Any SOC 2 exceptions or gaps from the last audit we should be aware of?
[04:40] Ravi Desai: The last Type II had a minor recommendation around change management documentation for one microservice; no major exceptions. We'll note the remediation plan and dates.
[04:52] Liam Chen: Data residency — can you guarantee EU-only hosting for a pilot? We need data to remain in EU for the POC.
[05:00] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we have EU regions and can pin the hosted endpoints to EU-only. For Dedicated or Private, you control region and network. We'll need to update the deployment config and the DPA to specify residency.
[05:15] Maya Patel: Encryption in transit and at rest — TLS? Customer key separation?
[05:20] Ravi Desai: TLS 1.2+ in transit, all data at rest is encrypted. Customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported; separation of duties is enforced — keys are not accessible to standard Redwood operators when BYOK is in place. For hosted we have HSM-backed providers as mentioned.
[05:40] Priya Rao: Do you have SOC 2 controls around personnel access and background checks?
[05:45] Jordan Park: Yes, personnel controls, background checks, least privilege and onboarding/offboarding are covered in SOC 2 and ISO artifacts. The Trust Center has HR policy summaries.
[05:56] Maya Patel: Can you provide an example of audit log retention configuration for enterprise? e.g., 365 days with S3 immutability?
[06:04] Sofia Martinez: We can export to S3 with object lock for immutability configured; our enterprise offering has that capability via our logging export pipeline. We'll include example configs.
[06:20] Liam Chen: On RBAC - is there an API for role changes and is it logged?
[06:25] Ravi Desai: Yes, admin events including role changes are logged with actor ID and timestamp; you can pull them from the audit exports. We log via secure append-only stores.
[06:40] Priya Rao: A note - our procurement team will want the ISO scope doc and evidence index before we proceed to a pilot.
[06:47] Jordan Park: We'll surface the scope and the evidence index in the Trust Center access; I'll start the access request process.
[06:55] Maya Patel: On the controls mapping, please call out shared vs Redwood-responsibility vs AlphaHealth responsibility.
[07:01] Sofia Martinez: Yep, each mapping row will include a 'responsibility' column.
[07:06] Liam Chen: For the KMS integration - rotation policies, do you have an automated rotation or do customers handle rotation in BYOK?
[07:13] Ravi Desai: For Redwood-managed keys we rotate per our internal schedule and notify customers; for BYOK you control rotation. We support automatic rotation hooks if you want us to rotate keys in a connector, but keys remain under your control.
[07:30] Maya Patel: Is there support for HSM-backed on-prem for the private deployment?
[07:35] Sofia Martinez: For Private on-prem we provide integration points to your HSM or KMIP appliances; our ops package includes connectors and docs.
[07:44] Priya Rao: What about penetration testing and VAPT reports?
[07:48] Jordan Park: We do annual VAPT and third-party pen tests; summary reports are available in the Trust Center and full technical reports can be shared under NDA and usually after a request.
[08:00] Liam Chen: Any SLAs around forensic timelines if there's a suspected data event?
[08:05] Ravi Desai: Our incident response SLA for enterprise includes initial acknowledgement within 1 hour, triage within 6 hours, and a forensic timeline depending on scope; details are in the incident response playbook. We'll include a redacted playbook sample.
[08:20] Maya Patel: Ok, sounds like a lot to digest. Can you walk through an example control mapping for encryption?
[08:26] Sofia Martinez: Sure- for example, encryption at rest maps to SOC 2 CC6 and ISO A.10/A.14 controls; in the mapping we'll show control statement, Redwood implementation notes, and who owns key rotation (Redwood vs customer).
[08:40] Priya Rao: Are there any material differences between SOC 2 and ISO coverage we should note?
[08:45] Ravi Desai: Generally SOC 2 is focused on Trust Services Criteria and operational controls; ISO is broader, covering ISMS, risk mgmt, and few additional clauses. We'll surface any coverage gaps and a remediation timeline if needed.
[08:58] Jordan Park: Quick note: some product names in our older docs might have small typos (e.g., 'Redwood Console' sometimes shown as 'Redwood Control'), apologies, but the latest docs are cleaned.
[09:10] Maya Patel: Good to know. For Trust Center access - what's the request flow?
[09:15] Jordan Park: I'll send an access request link; you'll need to submit corporate email list and a signed DPA + NDA. After review, we provision read-only Trust Center access.
[09:27] Priya Rao: Will evidence include raw logs or just attestations?
[09:31] Ravi Desai: Mostly attestations and evidence indices; raw logs for security reasons are provided in controlled ways (e.g., limited sample) and usually require justification.
[09:45] Liam Chen: For our SIEM integration, do you support syslog forwarders or only cloud storage?
[09:50] Sofia Martinez: We support multiple export mechanisms: S3/GCS exports, syslog/forwarders to customer endpoints for Dedicated/Private, and streaming connectors to common SIEMs.
[10:05] Maya Patel: Anything in the SOC 2 that references third-party subprocessors we should know?
[10:11] Jordan Park: Yes, cloud infra providers and some monitoring vendors are listed as subprocessors; full list is in the Trust Center and in the DPA.
[10:20] Priya Rao: One more item - can you produce evidence of background checks for specific operator accounts?
[10:26] Ravi Desai: We can provide redacted evidence confirming background check policies and attest that operators have completed checks, but we can't share raw PII of employees.
[10:37] Jordan Park: Ok, want to talk about timelines for the deliverables? We'll aim to share SOC 2 and ISO cert links within 3 business days and controls mapping draft in 4 business days.
[10:48] Maya Patel: That timeline works for us. We'll also need a technical deep dive on KMS and audit logs after we review the mapping.
[10:55] Sofia Martinez: Let's tentatively schedule that deep dive next week; we'll poll calendar availability after I send the controls mapping.
[11:05] Priya Rao: Anything else from AlphaHealth?
[11:08] Maya Patel: Not from me — procurement will follow up on DPA.
[11:12] Liam Chen: No, thanks.
[11:13] Jordan Park: Great — recap and next steps: I'll send SOC 2 Type II, ISO cert, Trust Center access instructions; Sofia/Ravi will share controls mapping and sample audit export; schedule a KMS/audit-log deep dive.
[11:25] Maya Patel: Thanks Jordan, appreciate it.
[11:27] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone.
[11:30] End of meeting.

Notes: transcription has minor errors (product name typos, occasional filler words) consistent with Fireflies exports. The team agreed on next steps and action owners.
